- description: "A bending beam load cell, with strain gauges. Registered trade name: 3S Fabrications"

Characteristics (type level):
- characterization_of_load_cell_capabilities: "Analog-passive load cell" — this is more of a module designation. Could be recorded in type_level or as module_designation.
- maximum_capacity: Emax range "50 kg up to and including 200 kg" → value {min: 50, max: 200}, unit kg. Is this a model matrix? It's a range covering capacities, single model ZNS with capacities from 50 to 200 kg. This is a range, not a family of models. So type_level with {min: 50, max: 200}.
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg
- accuracy_class: "C" (string)
- rated_output: 2.30 mV/V ± 0.23 mV/V → value 2.30, unit mV/V, tolerance ±0.23 mV/V. How to express? Could be value: 2.30, unit_symbol: "mV/V", with tolerance. Schema doesn't have tolerance field; keep value as {min: 2.07, max: 2.53}? Hmm. Better: value: 2.30, unit_symbol: "mV/V", plus a separate note? The structured rules say numbers. Tolerance isn't covered. I could set value: {min: 2.07, max: 2.53} since ± 0.23 means range. But that loses the nominal. Alternatively record rated_output: 2.3 mV/V and rated_output_tolerance: 0.23 mV/V. I think splitting is cleaner: rated_output value 2.30, and rated_output_tolerance 0.23. Both unit mV/V.
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 3000 (with footnote marker 1)
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 10000 (footnote 1)
- ratio_z_emax_over_dr: 3000 — actually Z = Emax / (2 * DR). Canonical: ratio_z... I'll call it ratio_z_emax_over_2dr? The rules example: "Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval(1) Y=Emax/vmin" → ratio_y_emax_over_vmin. So for Z: ratio_z_emax_over_2dr. Hmm, maybe ratio_z. I'll use "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr". Actually simpler: ratio_z. Let me follow the pattern: ratio_z_emax_over_2dr seems awkward. Maybe "ratio_of_minimum_dead_load_output_return_z" — but canonical snake_case example suggests formula-based naming. I'll use "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr". Hmm, could also be "ratio_z". I'll go with "ratio_z" ... no, follow pattern strictly: ratio_y_emax_over_vmin for Y, so ratio_z_emax_over_2dr for Z. I'll use that.
- input_impedance: 410 Ω ± 30 Ω → value 410, unit "Ω", tolerance 30. Again split: input_impedance 410 Ω, input_impedance_tolerance 30 Ω. Or value {min: 380, max: 440}. I'll do nominal + tolerance split for consistency.
- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7
- humidity_class: "NH"
- safe_overload: 150 % of Emax → value 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- output_impedance: 350 Ω ± 5 Ω → nominal 350, tolerance 5
- recommended_excitation: 5 V AC/DC → value 5, unit "V", plus type AC/DC? Could add excitation_type: "AC / DC". Keep as value 5 V and separate recommended_excitation_type "AC / DC". Hmm, maybe just record value 5, unit V, and a second characteristic. Simpler: recommended_excitation: value 5, unit_symbol "V". Add recommended_excitation_type: "AC / DC". Similarly excitation_maximum: 15 V, type AC/DC.
- transducer_material: "Stainless steel"
- atmospheric_protection: "Silicon potting"

Footnotes: The remarks: "1. The characteristics for n_max, Y and Z can be reduced separately." This is a remarks numbered list, corresponding to the (1) markers on n, Y, Z rows. So footnote marker "1)" text "The characteristics for n_max, Y and Z can be reduced separately." I'll include footnote with marker "1)".

Recommendation: id "R60", edition... "OIML R 60-1:2021". Hmm, R60-1 is part 1 of R60. Edition 2021. The schema: id canonical e.g. "R60", edition (int), amendment, scheme, accuracy_classes[]. Edition int — 2021 is a year not edition number. R60 2021 edition. edition: 2021. accuracy_classes: ["C"]. scheme: "A" (this is the certificate scheme). I'll put scheme "A".

Test reports: No. NMi-4032553-01 dated 20 July 2026, 50 pages, role: type_evaluation_report.

Revision history: revision "0", date 2026-07-20, changes "Initial issue."

Model family: not >1 model variant — single type ZNS with capacity range 50–200 kg. No model_family needed. Actually the range 50–200 kg — capacities between? It could be interpreted as multiple capacities, but likely a range. Keep type_level as range.
